newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan phone law will take effect in November.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan phone law will take effect in November.

text.p: A new law opening up Guatemala's state-owned telecommunications industry to international competition will take effect in November, a congressman said Tuesday.

"The executive branch needs to sign and publish the law. Within about 20 days it will be in effect," Mario Roberto Paz, president of the congressional telecommunications committee, told Reuters in an interview.
The 80-member congress passed the law Thursday with 43 votes in favor.
The Guatemalan Telecommunications Company Guatel does not have the millions of dollars it needs to keep up with an unsatisfied demand for more than one million telephone lines.
Under the current system Guatemalans pay for a new line and then wait up to 18 months for installation.
"The most important thing about the law is that it opens up the telecommunications market to other businesses that aren't Guatel, so that they can provide service," said Paz.
The first draft of the law, as presented by the majority National Advancement Party, proposed the creation of an autonomous entity which would oversee the industry.
But the party couldn't get the two-thirds majority vote needed to create the entity.
As passed, the law creates a Superintendency of Communications which will be named by the Communications Minister and will be funded by a percentage of income of all businesses in the industry.
The superintendency will also manage a fund to subsidize phone lines to remote areas.
The same body will be in charge of regulating the industry, mediating disputes, and bringing sanctions against companies that disobey the law.

According to the new law, the superintendency will regulate prices for basic services, but all other prices will be subject to the free market. Private companies will negotiate their own interconnections to other networks.

The proposed law doesn't set a maximum foreign ownership of the telecommunications industry in Guatemala. Minimum investment amounts will be set for each individual frequency or area opened up for bidding.
